## How it works

- [statement] The paper's model lineup changed between revisions (v2 lists GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.7, Grok 4.2, DeepSeek V3.2; latest lists GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, Grok 4.3, DeepSeek V4 Pro), so tic measurements are tied to a specific model version and get re-run when versions ship. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-05) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19139 · keywords: Tic drift across model versions · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2
- [statement] Juzek and Ward (COLING 2025) found no evidence that overrepresented words like 'delve' stem from model architecture, algorithm choice or training data, and tested RLHF as a candidate cause, so the mechanism behind version-to-version drift is unresolved. (low confidence) — https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.426/ · keywords: Tic drift across model versions

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Verbal Tic Index paper scores eight frontier models over 160,000 responses (10,000 prompts, English and Chinese); VTI ranged from 0.590 (Gemini 3.1 Pro, highest) to 0.295 (DeepSeek V4 Pro, lowest) in the latest revision. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-05) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19139 · keywords: Tic drift across model versions
- [statement] Rudnicka and Juzek find linguistic patterns shifted measurably between 2024 and 2026 model cohorts, and models of the same generation differ sharply (contraction rate from over 1,200 to over 30,000 per million words). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06589 · keywords: Tic drift across model versions
